title: Light upon light
hookLine: the Verse of Light: God is the light of the heavens and earth, a lamp in a niche
carry: almost glowing before the fire arrives

cards: A small hollow set into a wall. Inside it, a lamp. Around the flame, a glass so clear it shines like a star.
The oil comes from an olive tree, and it would almost glow on its own, even if no fire touched it. That's the whole scene: a lamp in a niche. It sounds like a room in an old house at night.
But it's in the Quran, the likeness it gives for God's light, and it's known as the Verse of Light.

teach.h: THE LIGHT OF THE HEAVENS AND THE EARTH.
teach.b: First, the size of it. The verse opens as big as a sentence can get. In Pickthall's translation: "Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth."
Not a light in the sky. The light of all of it. Second, the shrinking.
Right after that huge opening, the verse gives a likeness, a picture, and the picture is tiny: a niche, a lamp, a glass, an olive tree.
The tree, it adds, is neither of the east nor of the west; it belongs to no one direction.

teach.h: SHOWN AT THE SIZE OF A LAMP.
teach.b: So the light that fills everything is shown at the size of something you could hold in your two hands. Third, the layers. The niche holds the lamp.
The glass makes the flame shine like a star. The oil is already almost glowing before the fire arrives.
Each piece adds to the brightness.
Then the verse sums it up in three words: "Light upon light." Fourth, who sees it. The verse goes on to say that God guides to His light whom He will, and that God speaks to people in likenesses.
Readers have heard the layers in different ways. Some see the niche as the human heart, and the lamp as what shines inside it. Others keep it as a picture of God that no explanation fully opens.
The verse itself doesn't decode the picture. It hands you the lamp and lets you look.

how: Muslims recite the Verse of Light (Quran 24:35) in prayer and study, and commentators and Sufi writers have reflected on what the niche, the glass, the lamp and the oil might stand for.

o: a shelf in a mosque where the Quran is kept
a small cave where a prophet went alone to pray
the hollow that holds the lamp in the Verse of Light

games.q: inside the Verse of Light — tap the pairs.
p: neither of the east nor of the west
would almost glow with no fire

s: the verse begins with the lamp
it begins as big as it can: "Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth." the lamp comes after.
the verse says it is giving a likeness, a picture
it offers the lamp in the niche as a likeness of God's light.
the olive tree in the verse belongs to the east
the verse says it is neither of the east nor of the west.

games.q: you have to describe a light that fills the heavens and the earth. which picture do you reach for?
o: a small lamp in a niche in a wall.
games.why: the verse reaches for a lamp in a niche: the light of everything, shown at the size of something you could hold.

practice: Light one candle, or switch on one lamp and turn the others off, or find the brightest small thing in the room, even a patch of daylight on the wall.

Let your eyes rest on the layers: the flame or the bulb, the glow around it, the light it throws on things nearby. If you pray, you can hold the verse's opening words; if not, just watch the light do what it does.
